texts: Bivalirudin is the most appropriate alternative anticoagulant: A.
A fall in platelets from 125,000 to 42,000 on heparin suggests heparin-induced thrombocytopenia, so all heparin is stopped and a direct thrombin inhibitor is started.
Bivalirudin is cleared mostly by enzymes in the blood and only partly by the kidneys, so it suits a patient with both renal and liver dysfunction.
Argatroban is cleared by the liver, lepirudin by the kidneys, enoxaparin cross-reacts with heparin antibodies, and warfarin must not be started while the platelets are low in acute HIT.
In the picture, the black leech is chosen, the hare is sent away and the white plates come back.
Memory hook: when the kidneys and the liver both fail, call the leech the blood itself clears.
